objective: Prove: in a loop of four rule-60 rings with each contact reading its left neighbours (law 12) or both neighbours (law 6) on both rings, the second-order feedback cancels exactly when the contacts' positions sum to 2s, giving each contact a closed form; under a no-overlap condition every contact then binds both rings at every lag at every size, and each contact needs the two rings it does not touch at lags given by binomial coefficients mod 2.
status: Proved 2026-11-08 (by hand; finite claims checked): in loops of four rule-60 rings with contacts reading their left neighbours (or both neighbours) on both rings, the returning feedback cancels exactly when the contacts' positions sum to 2s, giving each contact a closed form over GF(2); then, under a no-overlap condition, every contact binds both its rings at every lag at every ring size, and each contact needs the rings it does not touch at binomial lags. Covers 16 of LOOP-RINGS's 54 families; the other 38 (overlapping partners, mixed laws) and unbalanced loops are where the argument stops.
title: Feedback cancels in balanced loops
